On jumping made contact with FLOWING RICHES due to both runners shifting ground.  When questioned regarding his riding of GOLDEN ACE, which was having its first race start, E Brown stated that his instructions were to settle the horse where comfortable and he was given no other instructions in relation to where to position the horse during the event.  He said after being bumped at the start he did not ride his mount along in the early stages to allow it to balance and settle where comfortable in accordance with his instructions.  When questioned if there was an opportunity to encourage his mount to hold a more forward position Jockey Brown stated that as the horse raced greenly he elected to allow it to settle towards the rear of the field where it was travelling comfortably.  He added that throughout the middle stages GOLDEN ACE continued to race greenly and entering the course proper near the 400 Metres became unbalanced.  He said when positioned behind and to the outside of GOOD POWER near the 400 Metres he contemplated shifting to the inside of that runner to follow LAHORE but elected to remain racing behind JUICY DRAGON as he was of the opinion that horse was travelling well enough to provide him with a horse to follow into the event.  When questioned if there was an opportunity to ride the horse with more vigour between the 400 Metres and the 200 Metres Jockey Brown stated that as he was still assessing where he was going to improve he continued to encourage his mount forward but not applying full vigour which allowed GOLDEN ACE to improve behind JUICY DRAGON.  He said when JUICY DRAGON did not improve as he had expected this resulted in GOLDEN ACE being badly held up for clear running behind JUICY DRAGON between the 200 Metres and the 150 Metres before he was able to shift to that runner’s outside to secure clear running.  He further stated that from this point on GOLDEN ACE finished the race off well under hard riding.  Trainer C Fownes confirmed the instructions issued and expressed satisfaction with Jockey Brown’s ride.  After considering his explanation the Stewards advised Jockey Brown that, in their opinion, he should have applied more pressure to the horse in the early stages to maintain a more forward position and secondly between the 400 Metres and the 200 Metres to ride his mount with more urgency to endeavour to improve to the inside of JUICY DRAGON earlier in the Home Straight.  Jockey Brown was advised that in future he should ride his mounts in a manner to leave no room for query.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.

Apprentice H Y Yuen stated that her mount was disadvantaged by the early and middle stages being run inside of standard time and as a result was left without a finishing effort in the Home Straight.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
Near the 900 Metres shifted out when being steadied to avoid LADY’S CHOICE.

Bumped at the start.  When questioned Y L Chung stated that his mount, which was having its first race start at Sha Tin, was stirred up prior to the event.  He said TYCOON RESOURCES jumped well and was able to obtain a handy position.  He said although the early and middle stages were run inside of standard time TYCOON RESOURCES travelled satisfactorily but when asked to improve on the Home Turn did not respond to his riding and gave ground in the Home Straight.  Trainer A S Cruz advised the horse had pleased him leading into the race and confirmed the advice of Jockey Chung that the horse was stirred up prior to the running of tonight’s event.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race revealed that the horse was displaying an irregular heart rhythm.  Before being allowed to race again, TYCOON RESOURCES will be required to perform satisfactorily in a barrier trial and be subjected to an official veterinary examination.  Sent for sampling post-race.
